test_title: PYST 17: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jun, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question:
A trader offers to sell a commodity under any of the two schemes mentioned below:

Scheme 1: The trader offers two successive discounts of 20% and 12.5% on the sale of each unit.

Scheme 2: The trader offers the buyer an option to ‘pay for y units, get z units free’. The buyer realizes that if he needs to buy (y + z) units, it does not matter to him which of the two schemes he opts for.

Which of the following options gives a correct ordered pair of (y, z)?
solution:
**Concept used:**

Effective discount = D₁% + D₂% - (D₁% × D₂%)/100

**Calculation:**

Scheme 1:

Effective discount% = 20 + 12.5 - (20 × 12.5)/100

⇒ 32.5 - 2.5 = 30%

Scheme 2:

⇒ (z × 100)/(y + z) = 30%

We need to check it by option:

If we put y = 3 ; z = 7 then

⇒ (7 × 100)/(10) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 7 ; z = 10 then

⇒ (10 × 100)/(17) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 10 ; z = 7 then

⇒ (7 × 100)/(17) ≠ 30%

If we put y = 7 ; z = 3 then

⇒ (3 × 100)/(10) = 30%

So the value of y = 7 & z = 3 satisfies the equation.

**∴ The correct option is 4. **
